brief: Zero Hedge's weekly wrap frames the week as a 'doom loop': oil sets inflation expectations, which set the Treasury long end, which prices everything except AI megacaps. Iran/Houthi attacks near Hormuz plus Hurricane Isaias cutting 63% of Gulf oil output pushed Brent to $106; Trump's pledge not to strike Iran before the midterms and a diesel deal with Putin pulled it back to $103. Despite three strong Treasury auctions, the 10-year held near 5.25-5.36%; Goldman says real rates and a shift in the marginal buyer from insurers to levered money exiting explain it, not inflation fear. September Fed minutes showed unanimous support for the hike, 'most' wanting another by year end (~80% December odds), and some officials linked higher long yields partly to AI-related borrowing. That crowding-out thesis met equities Thursday when the FT reported OpenAI's annualized revenue near $50bn, $20bn below the $68-70bn figure circulating weeks earlier, a gross-vs-net accounting gap; Nasdaq, SOX, Oracle, Broadcom, Nvidia and CoreWeave sold off and Oracle's CDS hit a record, before a Bloomberg report of $70bn by year-end lifted stocks back to flat. Brazil's Bolsonaro beat Lula in round one, sending the Ibovespa up 7.7%; investors put $166bn into money-market funds, the largest weekly inflow since April 2020.
